item.title: The Swannanoa Gathering Public Concerts — Mon Jul 20, 7:30 PM — Warren Wilson College Swannanoa
item.description:
The Swannanoa Gathering was established in 1992 as a vision of Warren Wilson College President Doug Orr and founding Director Jim Magill to host summer workshops celebrating the music and dance traditions of the southern Appalachian region and beyond.
Big news…Our staff concerts will now be open to the public!
We’re excited to be able to share our incredibly talented staff with Asheville and the surrounding Western North Carolina community. Tickets will be available for purchase online and at the door.
The Swannanoa Gathering is an educational program of the college, consisting of a series of week-long workshops in various folk arts held on the campus of Warren Wilson College just east of Asheville in the heart of North Carolina’s beautiful Blue Ridge Mountains. Tickets are $35 per concert. Event Details & Tickets https://swangathering.com/about-us/public-concerts/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.description:
Asheville Tech Events ## Details
Join us for our monthly project/co-working day! Bring your own project for co-working or jump in on an existing project. We can use all different kinds of support, from emailing to data entry to coding.
**Location:** Hi Wire Brewing - Biltmore Village / Guajiro Cuban food truck 2A Huntsman Pl, Asheville, NC 28803
**What to expect:** (Feel free to drop in when you can and leave when you need to.)
* *11am*: Arrival and introductions. Say hi and catch up with your Code with Asheville crew. * *11:15-11:30am*: Folks chat through what they hope to accomplish for the day, ask for help, and divide into small groups for certain projects. This is a great place to get plugged in if you're looking for a project to work on. * *11:30am*: We get to work! Some of us stay in the main meeting chat room while we work, others go heads offline. * 1-2*pm*: Wrap up our work for that day until next time

item.title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville — Sun Aug 9, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

item.title: Let's Walk: It's Leaf Season at the NC Arboretum — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center. Restrooms are available at the start point. We will start walking as soon as everyone has arrived.
The walk is a guided 5 KM trail. There are some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. Some people will want walking poles.
We will walk down Wesley Branch Trail to Bent Creek Road. Traveling down Bent Creek Road, we will loop through the Azalea Garden a little further than we usually go. The Azaleas won't be in bloom, but it will be leaf season after all. We will continue down Bent Creek Road, returning to the parking lot via Wolf Branch Road and Greenhouse Way. Before we quit, we will walk through the Bonsai Exhibition Garden and the Formal Gardens.
Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack.
